meta: Peasants gather around a pipe-smoking mason in an inn: David Teniers the Younger's The Smoking Mason, in the Rijksmuseum.
about: Peasants gather in an inn around a seated mason who smokes a pipe. A dog sniffs at the tools lying on the floor, and a few figures stand by a fireplace in the background. The Rijksmuseum calls the picture The Smoking Mason. David Teniers the Younger painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1675.

meta: William Unger's 1847 print of The Sacrifice of Isaac, made after a painting by Jan Lievens.
about: William Unger made this print in 1847 after Jan Lievens's painting of the Sacrifice of Isaac. Lievens's painting is in the Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum in Braunschweig. The print is in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Vincenzo Vangelisti's 1777 portrait print of Philippe-Emmanuel, Count of Ligniville, probably made for a French book of famous lives.
about: Vincenzo Vangelisti made this portrait of Philippe-Emmanuel, Count of Ligniville, in 1777. The Rijksmuseum thinks the print may have been made for La France Illustre ou Le Plutarque Français, a book published in Paris between 1775 and 1790.

meta: Shepherdesses wash in the water below a ruined tower in Nicolaes Berchem's Italian Landscape, painted in 1656.
about: Shepherdesses wash in the water in the foreground of this Italian landscape, with a crumbling tower beyond. Nicolaes Pietersz Berchem painted it in 1656. The Rijksmuseum's description names only those two things, and the painting is in its collection.

meta: Three columns of the Temple of Castor and Pollux stand in Giuseppe Vasi's 1747 view of the Roman Forum.
about: Three columns of the Temple of Castor and Pollux still stand in Giuseppe Vasi's view of the Roman Forum. On the left is the Temple of Antoninus and Faustina, whose main chamber was turned into the church of San Lorenzo in Miranda. Santa Francesca Romana rises in the distance on the right. The print belongs to Vasi's series of views of Rome, ten volumes of twenty prints published between 1747 and 1761.

meta: A farmhouse family around a hearth fire, Harmanus Vinkeles's 1787 print for a book of letters about country life.
about: Harmanus Vinkeles made this print of a farmhouse interior with a family gathered around a hearth fire. It was made in 1787 as an illustration. It appeared in Anna Maria Post's book Het land, in brieven, published in Amsterdam by Johannes Allart in 1788.

meta: A woman pokes the fire under a copper pot in Jacob Vrel's Woman at the Hearth, painted in 1654.
about: A woman bends over to poke the fire under a copper pot in the hearth. Some plates and bowls stand on the mantel, and a chair and a foot warmer sit in front of the fire. Jacob Vrel painted it in 1654. The Rijksmuseum bought it with support from its committee for photo sales.

meta: A fishwife holds up a fish at Amsterdam's New Fish Market in Emanuel de Witte's painting of 1655.
about: A fishwife holds up a piece of fish at the New Fish Market in Amsterdam. A man in a hat stands at a stall nearby, and several kinds of fish lie on wooden boards in front of it. Emanuel de Witte painted the scene in 1655.

meta: A bird on a branch and a snake on the coat of arms of C. de Koning Tilly Haarlemmerolie, a small vignette by Isaac Vincentsz. van der Vinne, 1681.
about: A bird on a branch and a snake appear on the coat of arms of C. de Koning Tilly Haarlemmerolie. Isaac Vincentsz. van der Vinne made this small vignette in 1681, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Coenraet Waumans's 1662 portrait of Lothair of France, made for a book of portraits of the rulers of Holland.
about: This portrait of Lothair of France has a coat of arms and a four-line French caption with biographical details in the margin. Coenraet Waumans made it in 1662 for Les pourtraits des souverains princes et comtes de Hollande by C. Meyssens, published in Antwerp that year. The title page names Richard Collin as the engraver of the coats of arms.

meta: Two naked children look through a portfolio of drawings in a painter's studio: Hippolyte Michaud's The Little Art Lovers, 1840.
about: Two small naked children look through a portfolio of drawings in a painter's studio. A palette with brushes lies at the left, and a large painting hangs on the wall. Hippolyte Michaud painted it in 1840, and it is in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Pieter Wilhelmus van de Weijer's 1851 portrait of Johannes Hubertus van den Broek in military uniform with a knight's order.
about: The sitter wears a military uniform with a knight's order and a badge for fifteen years of service. Pieter Wilhelmus van de Weijer made this portrait print of Johannes Hubertus van den Broek in 1851. His signature is under the portrait, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A Dutch city waterfront with barges, a dome and a windmill in the distance: Jacob Maris's Cityscape of 1898.
about: This is a view of the waterfront of a large Dutch city, with water in the foreground and the buildings of the quay behind it. Barges are moored along the quay, and a round dome and a windmill stand in the distance. Jacob Maris painted it in 1898. Mr. and Mrs. Drucker-Fraser of Montreux gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: A woman lays out washing on a fenced bleaching field in Jacob Maris's A Bleaching Field of 1870.
about: A woman lays sheets or washing on the ground of a bleaching field closed off by a fence. Another woman stands by a water pump in the middle, and the houses and a church of a town rise behind. Jacob Maris painted it in 1870. The heirs of W.J. van Randwijk of The Hague gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Ships on the IJ in front of eastern Amsterdam's skyline, a 1771 print by Willem Writs.
about: Ships sail on the IJ in front of the profile of eastern Amsterdam. From left to right the skyline shows the VOC warehouses on Oostenburg, the Oosterkerk, the naval storehouse, the Montelbaanstoren, the shipyard cranes, the Schreierstoren and the tower of the Oude Kerk. Willem Writs made this print in 1771.

meta: The fifth group of the Delft procession of 1862, lithographed by Willem Bernardus IJzerdraat.
about: Statesmen and soldiers on foot, numbered 60 to 80, form the fifth group of the Delft procession of 1862. They represent the envoys of the sultan of Aceh meeting Prince Maurice and the States on 4 September 1602. Willem Bernardus IJzerdraat's print belongs to a folder of eight lithographs of the procession.

meta: A monk walks reading through a landscape in Hilmar Johannes Backer's 1835 title page print.
about: A monk walks through a landscape while he reads a book, with a walking stick in his right hand and a dog running ahead of him. Behind him stand a chapel of Mary and, farther off, a monastery. Hilmar Johannes Backer made the print in 1835 as the title page for C. Spindler's De Pelgrimaadje van een kloosterbroeder, published in Haarlem.

meta: An entrance gate of the palace complex at Fatehpur Sikri in British India: Marius Bauer's print of 1899.
about: Marius Bauer made this print in 1899 of one of the entrances to the palace complex at Fatehpur Sikri in British India. The Rijksmuseum's note describes only the gate, and the print is in its collection.

meta: A group of riders gallops down a street in Constantinople in Marius Bauer's 1889 print.
about: A group of riders gallops down a street in Constantinople. The number 50 is printed in mirror image along the bottom. Marius Bauer made the print in 1889, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A man walks past a merchant in a Damascus bazaar in Marius Bauer's 1889 print.
about: A man walks past a merchant in a bazaar in Damascus. The number 72 is printed in mirror image along the bottom edge. Marius Bauer made this print in 1889, and it is in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Dutch, English, French and American ships off Japan in 1864, painted by Jacob Eduard van Heemskerck van Beest.
about: Sailing ships and steamships of the Dutch, English, French and American squadrons lie off the coast of Japan, with several rowing boats among them. The scene records the expedition led by the French commander Constant Jaurès in September 1864. Jacob Eduard van Heemskerck van Beest signed and dated the painting 1864. The Rijksmuseum holds its pendant too.

meta: Houses along a canal in Venice with gondolas on the water, an 1873 print by Etienne Bosch.
about: Houses line a canal in Venice, and a few gondolas float on the water. Etienne Bosch made the print in 1873. The Rijksmuseum's note says only that, and the print is in its collection.

meta: A monk kneels at a lectern with a book in Jacob Maris's Praying Monk of 1864.
about: A monk kneels in prayer at a lectern with a book lying on it. Jacob Maris painted it in 1864. Mr. and Mrs. Drucker-Fraser of Montreux gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: A tired mother sleeps beside a cradle with a cat and a candle, in Jacob Maris's Tired Out of 1869.
about: A mother has fallen asleep in a chair beside a cradle with a sleeping child in it. A cat sits by the cradle, and a candle burns on a table behind her. Jacob Maris painted it in 1869 under the title Moe gewaakt, meaning tired from keeping watch. Mr. and Mrs. Drucker-Fraser of Montreux gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: A man walks the rocky coast at Douarnenez in Brittany in Bernard Essers's 1927 print.
about: A man walks with a stick on the rocky coast at Douarnenez, a town south of Brest in Brittany. A few trees grow on the shore, and moored sailing boats lie in the sea. Bernard Essers made the print in 1927.

meta: A bridge and entrance gate at the Loosduinseweg in Loosduinen, a 1916 print by Jacques Hartog.
about: A bridge with an entrance gate crosses at the Loosduinseweg, level with the house Rustenburg in the former village of Loosduinen. The village has been part of The Hague since 1923. Jacques Hartog made the print in 1916.

meta: Ducks on the ice for February on a calendar sheet by Theo van Hoytema, 1902.
about: Three ducks stand on the ice while three more dive into the water behind them. Birds and snowdrops fill the ornamental border, and there is a tear line at the top of the sheet. Theo van Hoytema made this print in 1902 as the February page of a calendar.

meta: A chair with a cushion and a footstool in Barbara Elisabeth van Houten's 1877 print.
about: A chair with a cushion stands beside a footstool. A book lies on the left next to the chair, and a cloth hangs over the back on the right. Barbara Elisabeth van Houten made this print in 1877, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A vase of tulips printed by Barbara Elisabeth van Houten in 1872, with a note on the pale tulips.
about: Barbara Elisabeth van Houten printed this vase with tulips in 1872. A note kept with the print says, in Dutch, that the pale tulips should print more clearly. It is in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: A pot of honesty plants, shown twice with the second image upside down, in Jan Mankes's 1914 print.
about: A pot with honesty stands in this print by Jan Mankes, and at the top of the sheet the same picture appears again, upside down. Mankes made it in 1914, and the Rijksmuseum holds the print.

meta: An older woman with a Bible warns a younger one at a table in a lithograph of 1839 from the Mielin workshop.
about: Two women sit at a table. The older one has a Bible in front of her and makes a warning gesture to the younger. The stone-printing workshop of C.W. Mielin made this print in 1839, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Cornelis Sebille Roos, Amsterdam art dealer, smiles in Adriaan de Lelie's 1815 portrait.
about: Cornelis Sebille Roos smiles in a bust portrait turned to the right. He was an art dealer and broker in Amsterdam and an inspector of the National Art Gallery at the Huis ten Bosch in The Hague. Adriaan de Lelie painted him in 1815.

meta: A surprise guest at the gate of a house in Willem Steelink II's 1887 print Unexpected Visit.
about: An unexpected guest stands by the carriage he arrived in, while the host and his wife welcome him at the gate. A thistle sprig marks the lower left margin. Willem Steelink II made this print in 1887.

meta: The knight Huön finds Almansaris on a couch in Willem Steelink II's 1888 print from Wieland's Oberon.
about: The knight Huön finds Almansaris lying on a couch. The scene comes from Oberon by Christoph Martin Wieland. A thistle sprig marks the lower left margin of Willem Steelink II's print, made in 1888.

meta: Jan Toorop's 1904 print of a girl playing the violin, used on the cover of his Amsterdam exhibition catalog.
about: A girl plays the violin in this print by Jan Toorop, titled for Charley Toorop. It served as the cover of the catalog for his exhibition of paintings, watercolors and drawings at the art dealer Frans Buffa and Sons in Amsterdam. The show ran from February to March 1904.

meta: Juan Galvez's 1808 print of the battle at the Puerta del Carmen in Zaragoza, from a series of 36.
about: Juan Galvez made this print of the battle at the Puerta del Carmen in Zaragoza in 1808. It belongs to a series of 36 prints about the French attacks on the Spanish city that year. The series was published between 1812 and 1814.

meta: A French attack at the Puerta de Sancho in Zaragoza in Juan Galvez's 1808 print.
about: A French attack at the Puerta de Sancho in Zaragoza fills this print, with the title and a line of Spanish text in the lower margin. It belongs to a series of 36 prints by Juan Galvez about the French attacks on the city in 1808, published between 1812 and 1814.

meta: Herman Hendrik de Quiter's 1679 portrait print of Niclas Zobel, first used in his book Icones legatorum.
about: Herman Hendrik de Quiter made this portrait of Niclas Zobel in 1679. The print was first used in his book Icones legatorum, published in Nijmegen that year. The Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: August Remy's 1841 portrait print of a man probably named Selbstherr.
about: August Remy made this portrait in 1841 of an otherwise unknown man, probably named Selbstherr. The Rijksmuseum holds the print, and its note says nothing more about the sitter, not even the full name.

meta: Princess Wilhelmina of Prussia meets her brother Frederick William II at Cleves in 1788, drawn by Willem Joseph Laquy.
about: Princess Wilhelmina of Prussia meets her brother, King Frederick William II of Prussia, at the country house of Willem van Spaen in Cleves on 9 June 1788. Prince William V stands on the right. Willem Joseph Laquy drew the scene that year.

meta: Two linked medallions with a portrait of Joannes Lami and Athena writing, a print by Carlo Gregori of 1754.
about: Two medallions hang joined by a chain. The upper one holds a portrait of Joannes Lami, and the lower one shows Athena writing with a quill. An owl sits under her bench. Carlo Gregori made the print in 1754.

meta: Two Japanese women in large hats walk past blossoming trees in Kamisaka Sekka's 1909 print Spring.
about: Two Japanese women in large hats walk past blossoming trees. Kamisaka Sekka made this print in 1909. The Rijksmuseum notes that its Japanese title, Yayoi, means the third month of the old Japanese calendar.

meta: Four Spanish knightly orders on one plate, a 1843 print by Willem Charles Magnenat for a history of orders of knighthood.
about: Four Spanish knightly orders share one plate. Two decorations of the Order of Saint Ferdinand sit at the top, and below them are the orders of Calatrava and of Saint James of the Sword. Willem Charles Magnenat made the print in 1843, and it is plate 39 in a history of orders of knighthood published in Amsterdam by J.B. da Cunha.

meta: Dirk Jurriaan Sluyter's 1845 portrait of Professor Samuel Muller, made for an Amsterdam student almanac.
about: Dirk Jurriaan Sluyter made this portrait of Professor Samuel Muller in 1845. It appeared in the Amsterdamsche studentenalmanak, volume 15, of that year. The Rijksmuseum holds the print, and its note gives no more about the sitter.

meta: A boy laces his skate on the ice while two girls with a push sled watch, in Dirk Jurriaan Sluyter's 1854 print.
about: A boy kneels on the ice to put on his skate while two girls beside a push sled watch. A fishing net hangs between two posts on the bank, and a mill stands behind. Dirk Jurriaan Sluyter made the print in 1854 for the yearbook Aurora, published in Haarlem.

meta: Saint Phillip Evans with a knife in his chest, a portrait print by Alexander Voet II of 1679.
about: Saint Phillip Evans has a knife in his chest in this portrait by Alexander Voet II, made in 1679. Evans died as a result of the Popish Plot and is counted among the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales.

meta: Three putti with farm tools, a beehive and a glass on a 1803 title page by Reinier Vinkeles for Loosjes's book on wealth and poverty.
about: Three putti stand in a mountain landscape on this title page. One is by farm tools, one by a beehive and one raises his glass. Reinier Vinkeles made the proof in 1803 for Adriaan Pietersz. Loosjes's book on wealth, the middle class and poverty.

meta: Four angels carry Mary up from her grave in Wierix's 1595 print of the Assumption.
about: Four angels carry Mary up from her grave to heaven, two of them holding palm branches. The dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above her, and a two-line Latin caption runs in the margin. This is a print of 1595 by Wierix.

meta: Nuremberg beneath the personifications of Asia and Europe, sheet 1 of a 1666 print by Dirk Eversen Lons.
about: The German city of Nuremberg lies below the personifications of Asia and Europe, who sit in the sky above it. Dirk Eversen Lons made this first sheet in 1666, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Executioners raise the cross with Christ nailed to it in Hans Witdoeck's 1638 print, the middle part of the Raising of the Cross.
about: Christ is nailed to the cross, with a sheet carrying his name in several languages hanging at the top. Executioners and soldiers set the cross upright in the ground while a crowd watches in the background. A two-line Latin dedication runs in the margin. Hans Witdoeck made this middle part in 1638.

meta: Saint Hubert kneels before a stag with a cross in its antlers in Nicolaes de Bruyn's 1614 print.
about: Saint Hubert kneels before a stag. While hunting on Good Friday he saw a stag with a cross between its antlers, and he converted at once. Hunting dogs lie in the foreground. Nicolaes de Bruyn made the print in 1614.

meta: The facade of the Palazzo Di Negro in Genoa, built for a doge, in a 1622 print by Nicolaes Ryckmans.
about: The facade of the Palazzo Di Negro stands on the Via San Luca in Genoa. It was built between 1585 and 1587 for Ambrogio Di Negro, doge of Genoa. Nicolaes Ryckmans made this print in 1622 for Palazzi di Genova, a book by Peter Paul Rubens and Ryckmans published in Antwerp.

meta: A male and a female fool in donkey-eared caps talk to each other in Hans Sebald Beham's early print.
about: A male and a female fool sit facing each other in conversation. Both wear fool's caps with large donkey ears and feathers. The man carries a phallus as his attribute, and insects fly in the air around them. Hans Sebald Beham made this print, which the catalog dates to 1510.

meta: Jacques de Bie's portrait of Adelheid of Paris, from a 1635 history of France.
about: Jacques de Bie's portrait of Adelheid of Paris appeared in François Eudes de Mézeray's Histoire de France, published in Paris in 1635. It probably first appeared in de Bie's own book of true portraits of the kings of France in 1634. The print was used again in later publications.

meta: Five cats and a bird in Martin Ferdinand Quadal's 1793 animal studies from nature, published in London.
about: Five cats and a bird share this print by Martin Ferdinand Quadal. It comes from his book A variety of Tame and Wild Animals Studies from nature, published in London in 1793. The Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Five sheep heads in Martin Ferdinand Quadal's 1793 animal studies from nature, published in London.
about: Five sheep heads fill this print by Martin Ferdinand Quadal. It belongs to the series A variety of Tame and Wild Animals Studies from nature, published in London in 1793. The Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A woman with a boy on her back watches another boy feed the hens, in Keisai Eisen's luxury surimono of 1825.
about: A woman carries a small boy on her back and watches her other son feed the rooster and the hen. A plum tree in blossom stands behind her, and three poems accompany the scene. Keisai Eisen made this surimono in 1825. The Rijksmuseum explains that a surimono is a luxury print that pairs an image with poems, often made for poets as gifts to friends.

meta: Prussian troops attack Muiden on 1 October 1787 in Jacob Willem Strunck's 1792 print.
about: Prussian troops under General Friedrich Adolf von Kalckreuth attack the town of Muiden on 1 October 1787, and Amsterdam militia under Colonel Mattha defend it. The Prussians are in the foreground, and the bombardment of the town is in the background. Jacob Willem Strunck made the print in 1792, one of seven prints of the fighting around Amsterdam.

meta: Saul meets a procession of prophets playing music in Gilliam van der Gouwen's 1728 print.
about: Saul meets a procession of prophets playing music and is seized by the spirit of God, as told in 1 Samuel 10. The caption runs in Hebrew, Latin, French, English, German and Dutch. Gilliam van der Gouwen made the print in 1728 as an illustration for a Bible picture book published in The Hague by Pieter de Hondt.

meta: Two skiers glide down the slopes of Mount Fuji in Koizumi Kishio's 1942 print.
about: Two skiers glide down the white slopes of Mount Fuji under a bright blue sky. Koizumi Kishio began his series of thirty-six views of the sacred mountain in 1940, a nod to Hokusai's famous prints of the 1830s. According to the Rijksmuseum, Allied bombing later made him flee. This print is dated 1942.

meta: A fat monk stands in hellfire with a glass, bottle and pipe at his neck, in Jacob Gole's 1724 print.
about: A fat monk stands facing us in a ring of fire. A glass, a bottle, a pipe and other things hang around his neck, and they show a life that was anything but sober. The print is one of 50 in a series on abuses by the Catholic clergy. Jacob Gole made it in 1724 as an illustration for a book on the overthrow of Christian morals.

meta: A monk sleeps on a chair with a blank paper on his chest in Jacob Gole's 1724 print.
about: A monk sleeps on a chair with his hands folded over his stomach and his eyes lowered. A blank piece of paper lies on his chest. Jacob Gole made the print in 1724, and it is one of 50 in a series on abuses by the Catholic clergy.

meta: An eagle stands over a fire in an oval frame of ornamental vines, a 1615 print called Fire by Hans Janssen.
about: An eagle stands over a fire in an oval framed by ornamental vines. Hans Janssen made this print, titled Fire, in 1615. The Rijksmuseum's note describes only the eagle and the fire, and the print is in its collection.

meta: Water personified by three putti with a fishing rod and a water squirt, a print by Johann Baptist Klauber, 1750.
about: Water is personified in rocaille ornament by three putti with a fishing rod and a water squirt. A gargoyle and a stream in a landscape surround them. Johann Baptist Klauber made the print in 1750.

meta: Air personified by three winged putti with a kite and a basket of doves, a print by Johann Baptist Klauber, 1750.
about: Air is personified in rocaille ornament in a landscape by three winged putti, one with a kite and one with a basket of doves. Johann Baptist Klauber made this print in 1750, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Christ on the cross surrounded by signs of the Resurrection in Hieronymus Wierix's allegorical print of 1565.
about: Christ hangs on the cross with Moses and King David at its foot on the left and Paul and John the Baptist on the right. Around them are signs of the Resurrection. An eagle sits above the cross and on the right, a hen with her chicks is at the bottom, and a phoenix is on the left. In the background Moses raises the bronze serpent. Hieronymus Wierix made this print in 1565.

meta: Magdalena Adriana van Haren, Princess of Hohenlohe-Langenburg, in profile in a round frame, François Gonord, 1794.
about: Magdalena Adriana van Haren, Princess of Hohenlohe-Langenburg, appears in profile in a round frame, bust turned to the left. François Gonord made this portrait print in 1794. The Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: An ornamental jug with a snail shell and a snail in rocaille frames, a print by Hieronymus Sperling, 1705.
about: An ornamental jug with rocaille decoration, a snail shell and a snail, framed by more rocaille. It carries the publisher's number 20. Hieronymus Sperling made the print in 1705, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A jetty and houses in the harbor of Enkhuizen, George Marinus Tamson's 1912 premium print for the St. Lucas society.
about: George Marinus Tamson made this print of a jetty and houses in the harbor of Enkhuizen. The sheet says it was a premium print of 1912 for the St. Lucas society, which encouraged visual artists. The Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Moritz Lang's 1649 portrait of Johann Franz, Baron van Kaiserstein.
about: Moritz Lang made this portrait of Johann Franz, Baron van Kaiserstein, in 1649. The Rijksmuseum thinks the print may come from Elias Widemann's book Honori sacrum, printed in Vienna in 1649.

meta: Ships on the IJ with the skyline of eastern Amsterdam behind, another impression of Willem Writs's 1771 print.
about: Ships sail on the IJ with the skyline of eastern Amsterdam behind them. The skyline runs from the VOC warehouses on Oostenburg through the Oosterkerk, the naval storehouse and the Montelbaanstoren to the shipyard cranes, the Schreierstoren and the tower of the Oude Kerk. Willem Writs made this print in 1771.

meta: Heavy people feast in a kitchen while a thin man with a bagpipe is chased out, in Hans Liefrinck's 1563 print The Fat Kitchen.
about: Heavy people feast on food and drink in a kitchen. Cooking and roasting go on at the hearth on the right. In front, two children play with food, a woman drinks while nursing a child, and a monk or priest drinks on the left. In the background a thin, poor man with a bagpipe is driven out of the door. Hans Liefrinck made it in 1563, and it has a pendant.

meta: A walker rests on a tree stump while a shepherd follows his flock, in Johannes Franciscus Hoppenbrouwers's 1847 tinted lithograph.
about: A walker rests on a tree stump while a shepherd and his dog follow a flock of sheep. Johannes Franciscus Hoppenbrouwers made this tinted lithograph in 1847. It is printed in black with beige and orange tone blocks and colored by hand.

meta: A town crier with a drum stands by a tree while people listen, in Bernhard Schreuder's 1776 print.
about: A town crier with a drum stands by a tree while people listen in the background. Bernhard Schreuder made the print in 1776. The sheet lies loose in an album, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Carlo Gregori's 1752 portrait print of the painter Bartholomeus van der Helst, after his self-portrait in the Uffizi.
about: Carlo Gregori made this portrait of the painter Bartholomeus van der Helst in 1752. It comes from Francesco Moücke's series of portraits of excellent painters who painted themselves, in the Imperial Gallery of Florence. It follows a self-portrait by Van der Helst in the Uffizi.

meta: Judas brings the 30 pieces of silver back to the high priests in Melchior Küsel's 1670 print.
about: Judas Iscariot brings the 30 pieces of silver back to the high priests and elders. German text runs in the lower margin, and the print is numbered 10 at the lower right. Melchior Küsel made it in 1670 as part of an album.

meta: A salt cellar held up by two male torsos growing from leafy vines, a print by Jean Lepautre.
about: The salt cellar is held up by two male torsos that grow out of leafy vines. Jean Lepautre's print is one of a series of six sheets. The catalog dates it 1628, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: An oval frame with a ship, an anchor and a sun behind clouds for Vander Meer, a print by Etienne Fessard of 1724.
about: An oval frame made for Vander Meer holds a ship and an anchor, with a sun behind clouds. Etienne Fessard made this print in 1724. The Rijksmuseum's note describes only that, and the print is in its collection.

meta: An angel wakes Peter in prison and leads him past the sleeping soldiers in Johann Sadeler's print of 1580.
about: An angel wakes Peter in prison. In the background the angel leads him out past the sleeping soldiers. A Latin caption gives the passage from the Acts of the Apostles, chapter 12. Johann Sadeler made this fourth print of a five-part series in 1580.

meta: Cannons and drilling soldiers on the Meidan-i-Shah square in Tehran, from Eugène Flandin's 1843 travel book on Persia.
about: Cannons stand lined up on the royal square in Tehran while a group of soldiers drills. The print is plate 23 from Voyage en Perse by the painter Eugène Flandin and the architect Pascal Coste, published in eight volumes in Paris between 1843 and 1854.

meta: The Palace of Char Bagh in Isfahan, plate 57 of Eugène Flandin's travel book on Persia, 1843.
about: This view of the Palace of Char Bagh in Isfahan is plate 57 from Voyage en Perse by the painter Eugène Flandin and the architect Pascal Coste. The book came out in eight volumes in Paris between 1843 and 1854, and the Rijksmuseum holds this plate.

meta: Two putti play a lute and a violin under a tree in Christoph Jamnitzer's 1573 landscape print.
about: Two putti sit at the foot of a tree in the middle, one playing a lute and the other a violin. The sheet belongs to a series of flat decorations with grotesques, cartouches, ovals, mascarons, putti and fantastic creatures. The series has three title pages, two text pages and 60 plates in three books. Christoph Jamnitzer made it in 1573.

meta: The Fountain of the Dômes in the garden of Versailles, a 1715 print by Antoine Hérisset.
about: Antoine Hérisset made this print of the Fountain of the Dômes in the garden of Versailles in 1715. It is numbered 20 at the lower right. The print was also used in Les Plans, Profils, Et Elevations, Des Ville, Et Château De Versailles, published in Paris by Gilles de Demortain.

meta: Dutch boats attack a Spanish Armada ship in Johannes Christiaan Bendorp's 1825 title page print.
about: Dutch boats attack a sailing ship of the Spanish Armada during King Philip II's failed attempt to invade England in 1588. Johannes Christiaan Bendorp made the print in 1825 as the title page for Jacobus Scheltema's book on the fitting out and fall of Philip's invincible fleet, published in Haarlem.

meta: Allegorical women around a bust of Peter Paul Rubens in Jean Antoine Pierron's 1791 print.
about: Allegorical women stand and sit around a bust of the painter Peter Paul Rubens on a pedestal. They include a woman playing a flute, one holding a broken column, one with four breasts, one with a painter's palette and one with an armillary sphere. A putto sits beside them with a bust and measuring tools, and an angel flies above to crown the bust. Jean Antoine Pierron made the print in 1791.

meta: Christ tells the parable of the wicked tenants under Scorpio in Adriaen Collaert's 1585 print for October.
about: Christ stands with two men at the left and points to the scene on the right, where the lord's son is murdered by the wicked vineyard keepers. Inside the fence, the lord's servants are beaten with sticks. The sign of Scorpio is at the top center, and four lines of Latin from Matthew 21 run below. Adriaen Collaert made the print in 1585 for October in an album.

meta: A brush-maker checks the tip of a brush in Hishikawa Sôri's surimono of 1803, with a girl playing ball.
about: A brush-maker checks the tip of a brush in his hand. A pot of different brushes stands in front of him, with a black lacquer box beside him, and a girl plays with a ball on the left. One poem goes with the picture. Hishikawa Sôri made this surimono in 1803, a luxury print that pairs an image with poems.

meta: James Gillray's 1799 English caricature of the Prince of Orange's expected return to Holland.
about: A stout Prince William V is surrounded by a cheering crowd and embraced and kissed by two fishwives, with frogs crawling at his feet. On the right, English troops land in small boats on the beach of North Holland. James Gillray made this English caricature in 1799 as a satire on the British and Russian invasion of that year.

meta: A ballerina by Louis Legrand, a print from the book Faune parisienne of 1901.
about: Louis Legrand made this print of a ballerina for Faune parisienne, a book by E. Ramiro and Legrand published in Paris by Gustave Pellet in 1901. The Rijksmuseum holds the sheet.

meta: Altars of the goddess Nehalennia on a sheet from Olivier de Wree's 1650 book, engraved by Jan de Mel in 1648.
about: This sheet gives an overview of altars of Nehalennia, numbered 10 to 18. Jan de Mel made it in 1648, and it comes from Olivier de Wree's Historiae comitum Flandriae libri prodromi duo, printed in Bruges in 1650. It is the second state, in which the page and number at the upper right were removed.

meta: Troops under Maarten van Rossum plunder The Hague in 1528, in Christiaan Lodewijk van Kester's print.
about: Soldiers under Maarten van Rossum plunder The Hague in 1528. Van Rossum sits on a horse in the middle, and soldiers with loot fill the foreground. Christiaan Lodewijk van Kester made the print in 1853 as plate 21 for Jacob van Lennep's history of the fatherland in sketches and pictures.

meta: Standard bearers and canons in Nicolaas Hogenberg's procession of Charles V and Pope Clement VII at Bologna in 1530.
about: Standard bearers and canons fill plate F of a frieze of 40 plates. It shows the procession of Charles V with Pope Clement VII at Bologna after the emperor's coronation on 24 February 1530. Nicolaas Hogenberg made it, and the Rijksmuseum keeps the plates pasted in an album.

meta: The Duke of Guise in the foreground of the Battle of Auneau, a 1587 print by Frans Hogenberg.
about: The Battle of Auneau was fought on 21 November 1587, and the Duke of Guise is in the foreground. Frans Hogenberg made the print the same year, with a sixteen-line caption in German below.

meta: The patriarch Zebulun with an anchor, a compass and a plumb line in Jacques de Gheyn II's 1587 print.
about: The patriarch Zebulun appears half-length with an anchor on his right arm, a compass in his right hand and a plumb line in his left. Houses, a harbor and a beacon stand behind him, a reference to the shore where Zebulun lived. Jacques de Gheyn II made the print in 1587 for a series of twelve patriarchs of Israel, each with a two-line Latin caption.

meta: Hecuba offers clothing to Minerva above three small scenes from the Trojan War, in a print by Luigi Ademollo of 1774.
about: Hecuba offers clothing to Minerva in the top picture. Below it, three small scenes from the Trojan War stand side by side, with an Italian caption in pencil. Luigi Ademollo made the print in 1774.

meta: A soldier opens a powder flask with his mouth, c. 1645, in Petrus Rucholle's musket drill print.
about: A soldier seen full length and facing right holds a musket against his left thigh with the barrel angled upward, and a musket fork in the same hand. With his right hand he lifts a powder measure to his mouth to open it. Petrus Rucholle made the print around 1645 as a new image, not copied from the usual musket drill instructions.

meta: Captain Lambert Hendriks has 125 captured Algerian corsairs hanged from the yardarms in Jan Luyken's 1682 print.
about: Captain Lambert Hendriks's ships lie off the coast of Algiers with the blood flag raised on the foremost one. 125 captured Algerian corsairs are hanged from the yardarms and thrown overboard tied together. This is said to have happened around 1619, to press for the release of captured ships and Christian slaves. Jan Luyken made the print in 1682.

meta: General Louis-Eugène Cavaignac seated in uniform with a cocked hat in a portrait print by Lévilly, 1848.
about: General Louis-Eugène Cavaignac sits facing us, shown to the knees, in military uniform with a cocked hat on his head. Lévilly made this portrait print in 1848, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: Twenty scenes from the life of the rogue Klaas Kapoen on one sheet, a colored woodcut by Philippus Jacobus Brepols, 1800.
about: One sheet carries 20 pictures of the life and doings of a rogue, Klaas Kapoen. Under each picture is a two-line verse in Dutch and French. Philippus Jacobus Brepols made the woodcut in 1800, colored in brown, yellow, green and red, and it is numbered 18 B.

meta: Gottlieb Freiherr von Thon-Dittmer in glasses, a half-length portrait print by Dominik Haiz of 1843.
about: Gottlieb Freiherr von Thon-Dittmer, who lived from 1802 to 1853, is shown half-length and facing us, wearing glasses. Dominik Haiz made this portrait print in 1843. The Rijksmuseum's note adds no more about the sitter.

meta: The Battle of Malplaquet on 11 September 1709, with the prince on horseback, a 1727 print by Jan van Huchtenburg.
about: The Allies under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy fight the French at Malplaquet on 11 September 1709, and the prince rides in on the left. Jan van Huchtenburg made the print in 1727 as an illustration in the first volume of Jean du Mont's book on the battles and sieges of three famous commanders.

meta: A harpooned whale lifts its tail above the water while harpooners ready to strike, in Adolf van der Laan's whaling print of about 1725.
about: A harpooned whale holds its tail above the water while harpooners stand ready to stab it in the side. Adolf van der Laan made the print around 1725 as part of a series on whaling. It is printed on the same sheet as number 6, and it is bound with a set of prints about herring fishing.

meta: A map of the Allied siege of Mons in 1709 by Jacobus Harrewijn, from a bound set of plans of the Spanish Succession war.
about: This is a map of the siege and capture of Mons by the Allies between 25 September and 22 October 1709. A cartouche at the lower right holds the title and a French key lettered A to I. Jacobus Harrewijn made it as part of a bound collection of plans of battles and cities from the War of the Spanish Succession.

meta: A town plan of Douai in 1709 by Jacobus Harrewijn, from a bound set of plans of the Spanish Succession war.
about: This is a plan of the city of Douai in 1709. Jacobus Harrewijn made it as one sheet of a bound collection of plans of battles and cities that became well known in the War of the Spanish Succession. The Rijksmuseum holds the collection.

meta: The actor Nakamura Utaemon IV as Danshichi Kurobei in Utagawa Kunimasu's 1850 print.
about: The actor Nakamura Utaemon IV plays Danshichi Kurobei in the play Natsumatsuri Naniwa kagami, performed at the Naka Theater in the fifth month of 1850. Utagawa Kunimasu made the print, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A triumphal gate at Brussels burned down the night after the entry of Charles Alexander of Lorraine in 1744.
about: A triumphal gate was put up for the entry of the governor Charles Alexander of Lorraine and his wife Maria Anna of Austria into Brussels on 26 March 1744. An inscription in pen says the gate burned down completely the night after the entry. François Harrewijn made the print.

meta: A triumphal gate in the Wijngaardstraat for William IV's inauguration at Veere in 1751, a print by Caspar Jacobsz. Philips.
about: This honorary gate stood in the Wijngaardstraat for the festive inauguration of the stadtholder William IV as marquis of Veere on 1 June 1751. Caspar Jacobsz. Philips made the print, numbered 2, for Andreas Andriessen's account published in Amsterdam by Isaak Tirion that year.

meta: The triumphal gate at the harbor of Veere with Neptune in his chariot, a 1751 print by Caspar Jacobsz. Philips.
about: The honorary gate by the harbor has Neptune in his chariots on the arch, with statues of Navigation and Commerce. It was part of the festive inauguration of the stadtholder William IV as marquis of Veere on 1 June 1751. Caspar Jacobsz. Philips made the print, numbered 4, for Andreas Andriessen's account.

meta: A French nobleman wrapped in his cloak waits for a happy adventure in Henri Bonnart's print of 1687.
about: A French nobleman faces us, wrapped in a loose cloak over his costume, with a broad-brimmed hat and plumes on his long hair. The French caption says that wrapped in his cloak this cavalier awaits some happy adventure. Henri Bonnart made the print in 1687.

meta: The comic figure Night Raven from a booklet of 36 odd figures, a print by Isaac Vincentsz. van der Vinne, 1731.
about: This comic figure is called Nachtraaf, or Night Raven, in the caption of the overview print. It belongs to a booklet of 36 odd figures invented by Izaak van Ostade of Haarlem, published in 1731 and 1732. Isaac Vincentsz. van der Vinne made the print.

meta: A stage set of the Abdy church with a scene from Robbert de Vries at the new Amsterdam theater, a print by Cornelis Brouwer of 1791.
about: The print shows a performance in the new Amsterdam theater, with the stage set of the Abdy church and a scene from Robbert de Vries. The set was printed from a separate plate inside a mount that shows the hall, the side boxes, the pillars with statues and the front of the stage. It belongs to a series of fourteen sets by Cornelis Brouwer for the theater.

meta: Uniforms of a lieutenant, a drummer and an auxiliary guardsman of the new Amsterdam civic guard, drawn by S.G. Casten.
about: This drawing shows the uniforms of a lieutenant, a drummer and an auxiliary guardsman of the new Amsterdam civic guard. S.G. Casten drew it for the second chapter of a sketchbook of colored drawings of uniforms of soldiers and guard members from 1770 to 1795.

meta: The first uniform of the cavalry of the Amsterdam exercise society in 1785, drawn by S.G. Casten.
about: This drawing shows the first uniform of the cavalry of the Amsterdam exercise society. S.G. Casten drew it for the second chapter of a sketchbook of colored drawings of uniforms of soldiers and civic guard members from 1770 to 1795, on the new Amsterdam guard of 1783 to 1787.

meta: Rafts and gunboats close off the Dordtsche Kil on 29 March 1793 against the French, a print by Carel Frederik Bendorp.
about: The Dordtsche Kil is closed off with rafts, gunboats and a few other vessels on 29 March 1793, as a defense against the French. Carel Frederik Bendorp made the print in 1793, and it has a pendant.

meta: A grotesque head made of plucked poultry with a helmet of dishes, after Arcimboldo, a print by Dominicus Custos, 1594.
about: A grotesque head has a face built from plucked poultry, with two dishes standing for a helmet and a ruff. A cloth is draped over the helmet. Dominicus Custos made this print in the style of Arcimboldo in 1594.

meta: Card players around a table with a French warning against gambling, women and wine, a print by Alexander Voet I of 1632.
about: Two men, and a man with a woman, sit around a table at cards, with money for the stakes lying on the table. The woman looks at the cards in the man's hand. A jug and a glass of wine stand on a tray, and a boy stands at the left. The French caption warns against gambling, women and wine. Alexander Voet I made the print in 1632.

meta: A crowing rooster in Pieter van Woensel's 1797 print for his almanac De Lantaarn voor 1798.
about: A rooster crows, facing left, with a two-line caption below. Pieter van Woensel made the print in 1797 as an illustration for his almanac De Lantaarn voor 1798, titled The Vigilant Rooster in the museum's catalog.

meta: People climb trees to escape the flood after the Lingedijk broke at Kedichem in 1809, a print by Jan Anthonie Langendijk.
about: The Lingedijk has burst at Kedichem during the flood of 30 January 1809. Several people climb into trees to escape the water, and groups flee on both sides of the breach. Jan Anthonie Langendijk Dzn made the print, and it has a pendant.

meta: British ships off Veere on 31 July 1809, with boats of soldiers rowing to the shore, a print by Friedrich Christoph Dietrich.
about: British ships lie off Veere in Zeeland on 31 July 1809, and boats carrying soldiers row from the ships to the shore. Friedrich Christoph Dietrich made the print in 1809, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A staircase of ages with men and women from 0 to 100 above the Last Judgment, a colored woodcut by Barend Koene III, 1814.
about: Men and women aged 0 to 100 stand on the steps of a staircase shaped like a bridge, a stair of old age. Under the bridge is a picture of the Last Judgment, with a putto at the lower left and Death at the lower right. The gate carries the text: Bedenkt den dagh die niet verblyen mag. Barend Koene III made this woodcut in 1814.

meta: One sheet of 14 scenes of soldiers' life, with fighting soldiers, Napoleon and a drummer, by J.J. Camphausen in 1843.
about: One sheet holds 14 pictures of a soldier's life, among them fighting soldiers, Napoleon and a soldier with a drum. J.J. Camphausen made the print in 1843, and it is numbered 35.

meta: Roemer Visscher's 1614 emblem 'T scheelt te veel, from Sinnepoppen, the first shock.
about: This print is emblem 23 from Sinnepoppen, a book of emblems by Roemer Visscher published in 1614. Its title is 'T scheelt te veel, and the Rijksmuseum notes it as the first shock of the series.

meta: One sheet of nine girls' games, including skipping rope and playing with dolls, a lithograph by Jan de Haan of 1875.
about: One sheet shows nine children's games for girls, including skipping rope and playing with dolls, each with a caption. Jan de Haan made this color lithograph in 1875, printed in yellow, green, orange, blue and red. It is numbered 4.

meta: John the Evangelist writes his gospel with an eagle beside him in Philips Galle's 1562 print.
about: The evangelist John writes his gospel with the eagle sitting beside him. John looks up to heaven, where Christ appears with a cross. A Latin text under the picture explains the scene. Philips Galle made this print in 1562, and it belongs to an album.

meta: A sheet of eight pictures of animals, plants and the Nile for biblical geography, a print by Jan Vlieger of 1871.
about: One sheet carries eight pictures of animals, plants and the Nile, each with a caption. Jan Vlieger made this print on biblical geography in 1871, and it is numbered 6.
